stories.headline: Russia warns 'hostile' Estonia is on the verge of open war
body: Russia's foreign ministry says Estonia's actions are 'on the verge of triggering open war'.
It summoned Estonia's envoy after Tallinn announced it would close its border with Russia.
Moscow also says Estonia let Ukrainian drones use its airspace; Estonia denies it.
stories.vc: Baltic tension adds risk for shipping and European markets.

stories.headline: US sanctions Iran's 'shadow banking' networks
body: The US Treasury sanctioned more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies and staff.
It says they move billions of dollars to get Iran foreign currency despite sanctions.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the system 'the last financial lifeline' of the regime.
stories.vc: Tighter money routes squeeze Iran's oil and petrochemical trade.

stories.headline: Bangladesh garment workers reject employers' pay offer
body: Worker representatives rejected factory owners' minimum-wage offer at Monday's wage board talks.
The board says the offer is above 14,500 taka ($116) a month; workers want 32,000 taka ($258).
The industry earns about $38bn a year and employs around four million people.
stories.vc: Higher wages or long strikes could raise clothing costs for global brands.

stories.headline: Sensex falls 1,484 points as bank stocks drag markets
body: The Sensex fell 1.77% to 82,435.99 and the Nifty fell 1.75% to 25,349.65.
Bank Nifty dropped 3.17% and metal stocks fell 3.68%.
IT stocks bucked the trend, rising 1.69%.
stories.joke: Banks had a bad day; coders had a good one.
stories.vc: A sharp fall hits mutual fund and PF portfolios across India.

stories.headline: RBI proposes a 'Stop Switch' to freeze payments during fraud
body: The RBI wants banks to offer a 'Stop Switch' that instantly disables all outgoing debits, new mandates and new UPI registrations.
Incoming money and existing standing instructions would keep working.
A 'Trusted Person' would add an extra check on big transfers. The rules would start July 1, 2027.
stories.joke: Finally, a panic button for your bank account.
stories.vc: Faster fraud controls could cut losses from digital payment scams.

stories.headline: Namma Metro ridership up 12%, fare revenue up 49%
body: Bengaluru's Namma Metro carried 310.49 million passenger journeys in 2025–26, up 12.29%.
Average daily ridership rose to 8.51 lakh, with a record 10.82 lakh on August 14, 2025.
Fare revenue jumped 49% to ₹1,125.58 crore.
stories.joke: Silk Board traffic: the metro's best salesman.
stories.vc: Rising fares and ridership help, but the metro still faces big finance costs.

stories.headline: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang as CEO
body: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned.
He had admitted affairs, one with a woman the US government suspects is a Chinese spy.
The board says it consulted senior US officials before deciding he is no security risk. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: The shortest CEO search in history.
stories.vc: Leadership certainty matters for the world's most valuable chipmaker.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion
body: Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal.
Zscaler sells cloud 'zero-trust' security to about 8,000 enterprise customers.
The firms say the deal positions them for the AI era. (No Economist piece was readable, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: Security, now in a bigger padlock.
stories.vc: Consolidation could give big companies fewer, larger security vendors to choose from.

stories.headline: Bret Taylor's Sierra doubles its valuation to $30 billion
body: Customer-service AI company Sierra raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round.
The valuation doubled from $15 billion in under six months.
It says it serves almost half the Fortune 50, including BNY, HSBC and Wells Fargo.
stories.joke: Customer service bots, now worth more than many banks they serve.
stories.vc: Investors are betting AI agents will replace large call-centre budgets.

stories.headline: Megaspeed, linked to the Nvidia scandal, faces a US blacklist
body: The US Commerce Department will add Megaspeed to its Entity List, Semafor reports.
Alice Huang, the woman at the centre of the alleged espionage scandal, led the firm for over two years.
US companies would need a special licence to sell to it. (Stratechery's new post is subscriber-only, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.vc: Blacklists can cut off chip sales and spook supply chains.

stories.headline: Steadview Capital sells Lenskart shares worth ₹921 crore
body: Hedge fund Steadview Capital sold 1.27 crore Lenskart shares at ₹725 each.
Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale bought them.
Early backers have sold at least ₹8,840 crore of Lenskart shares in three months. (No Unhedged piece was readable, so this is Inc42's report.)
stories.joke: Early investors see clearly: it's time to cash out.
stories.vc: Big institutional buyers stepping in signals confidence in Lenskart.

stories.headline: Rajasthan women's university to host a BRICS women's leadership centre
body: Banasthali Vidyapith, a women's university in Tonk, signed an MoU with BRICS nations on Monday.
The new centre will work on women's education and leadership worldwide.
It came at the end of a five-day BRICS women leaders' summit on campus.
stories.vc: Leadership training can open more senior jobs to women.

stories.headline: The anti-abortion movement faces a reckoning before 2028
body: Overturning Roe v. Wade could now help Democrats win the White House, The 19th reports.
A national abortion ban is so unpopular that many Republican front-runners avoid backing it.
Democrats could pass a law protecting abortion rights if they win the presidency and Congress.
stories.vc: Abortion policy affects women's health costs and where they choose to live and work.

stories.statLabel: GTA game with a required woman lead
stories.headline: GTA 6 puts a woman lead at the centre for the first time
body: For the first time in GTA history, a woman protagonist isn't optional.
Lucia Caminos, a Latina just out of prison, teams up with Jason Duval in a Bonnie-and-Clyde partnership.
The 19th says the game also explores love and relationships, not just violence.
stories.joke: Vice City finally hired a woman as co-lead.
stories.vc: Women leads can widen gaming's audience and sales.

stories.headline: Aster DM in talks to buy Narayana Health's north India hospitals
body: Aster DM Healthcare is in talks to buy Narayana Hrudayalaya's hospitals in north India for up to $150 million, Bloomberg reports.
Blackstone owns about 30% of Aster.
The deal would deepen Aster's push into India.
stories.vc: Consolidation can change prices and access for patients in north India.

stories.headline: AIIMS Bhubaneswar becomes India's third national burn-care training centre
body: AIIMS Bhubaneswar's burns and plastic surgery department will train doctors in burn injury care for the whole country.
The health ministry approved it under the national trauma and burns programme.
The department, now 10 years old, has treated over 1,500 burn patients.
stories.joke: Training the people who heal the worst injuries.
stories.vc: More trained burn specialists means better survival after fires and accidents.

stories.headline: Karnataka plans antibiotic audits in hospitals to fight superbugs
body: Karnataka's 2026–2030 plan against antimicrobial resistance proposes prescription audits in hospitals.
It also wants stricter curbs on over-the-counter antibiotic sales.
Nearly three in four Gram-negative bacteria samples resisted ceftriaxone, a common antibiotic.
stories.vc: Resistant infections make hospital stays longer and costlier.

stories.headline: LSEG Workspace adds Kalshi prediction-market data
body: Kalshi has put its prediction-market data into LSEG Workspace.
Users get real-time prices and probabilities for more than 25,000 event outcomes.
Categories include elections, politics, economics and financials.
stories.joke: The trading screen now has a crystal ball.
stories.vc: Institutional interest in prediction markets is growing fast.

stories.headline: Supertake raises $20M for AI agents that turn market 'takes' into portfolios
body: Supertake lets people turn their market ideas into real investment portfolios using AI trading agents.
Its $20 million seed round was led by Adjacent.
Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures also invested.
stories.joke: Hot takes, now with a brokerage account.
stories.vc: Automated agents could bring algorithmic trading to everyday investors.

stories.headline: Explainer: What is a prediction market?
body: Imagine your class trades cards that pay one sweet if it rains tomorrow, and nothing if it doesn't.
If a card sells for 70% of a sweet, the class thinks rain is about 70% likely.
That's a prediction market: the price works like a guess of how likely something is.
Kalshi runs markets like this on real events, like elections and the economy.
This week, LSEG put Kalshi's live prices on its screens for big investors.
stories.vc: Odds help traders see what crowds expect.

stories.headline: Verstappen is looking into racing the 2027 Daytona 24 Hours
body: Max Verstappen visited Daytona before the Las Vegas GP to film with Red Bull.
He says a 2027 entry is being looked into: 'That's definitely one that I want to do.'
He would race a GT3 car, in the GTD Pro class, during F1's winter break.
stories.joke: Max's idea of a winter holiday: 24 hours of racing.
stories.vc: A star F1 entry would be a big draw for US sportscar racing.
